The limited prayer of the petitioner, who is faced with a demand
for arrears of motor vehicle tax dues, is for the grant of installments
to enable her to discharge the liability in Ext.P3 demand notice.

the learned Government Pleader for the respondent.
On a consideration of the facts and circumstances of the case as

of financial hardship urged on behalf of the petitioner, I direct that if
the petitioner pays the amount demanded in Ext.P3, together with
accrued interest from 18.8.2016, in ten equal and successive monthly
installments commencing from 10.7.2017, then the further

Counsel for Petitioner :- Azhar Hussain
Counsel for Respondent :- G.A.
Hon'ble Ramesh Sinha,J.
Hon'ble Raj Beer Singh,J.
Heard Sri Azahar Hussain, learned counsel for the petitioner, Sri
G.P. Singh, learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the impugned
FIR as well as material brought on record.
This petition has been filed by the petitioner with a prayer to quash
the FIR dated 16.7.2019, registered as case crime No.0379 of 2019,
under Section 2/3 U.P. Gangsters and Anti Social Activities
(Prevention) Act, 1986, P.S. Malpura District Agra.
Learned counsel fo
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
gned FIR under the Gangster Act has been lodged
against the petitioner, the impugned FIR under the Gangster Act has
been lodged against the petitioner. He further submits that the
petitioner is neither a member of any gang nor he runs any gang
involved in anti-social activities. The allegation levelled against the
petitioner is absolutely false, frivolous and baseless. No offence is
made out against the petitioner, hence the FIR is liable to be quashed
by this Court.
Learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer for quashing of the F.I.R. which
discloses cognizable offence.
Considering the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the
parties and nature of the allegations, it is directed that the petitioner
shall not be arrested in above mentioned case, till the submission of
the police report under section 173(2) Cr.P.C. but he shall co-operate
with the investigation of the case.
It is made clear that if there appears to be any other case found
against the petitioner except the case mentioned in the Gang Chart
earlier to lodging of the present FIR, the present order granting
interim protection to the petitioner shall automatically stands
discharged.
With the above direction, this petition is finally disposed of.
Let a copy of this order be produced before the SSP concerned by
the petitioner within 10 days from today.
(Raj Beer Singh,J. ) (Ramesh Sinha, J.)

MAHESH GROVER, J.
Crl.Misc.No.1255 of 2013 is allowed.
This is a petition under Section 482 of the Code
of Criminal Procedure praying for directions to respondents No.1 to 3
to protect their life and liberty which is alleged to be in danger at the
hands of respondents No.4 and 5 on account of their having got
married against their parental consent.
Learned counsel for the
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
4 of 2013 (O&M) -2-
are as under :-
“In such cases of intercaste or inter-religion marriage
the Court has only to be satisfied about two things :
(1) that the girl is above 18 years of age, in which
case, the law regards her as a major vide Section 3
of the Indian Majority Act, 1875. A major is
deemed by the law to know what is in his or her
welfare.
(2) The wish of the girl.
In the circumstances, we direct that nobody will
harass, threaten or commit any acts of violence or other
unlawful act on the petitioner, Chanchali Devi/Mehvesh
Anjum and the petitioner's family members and they shall
not be arrested till further orders in connection with the
case in question. If they feel insecure, they can apply to
the police and, in such event, the police shall grant
protection to them.”
In view of this, the petition is disposed of with a direction
to respondent No.2 to look into the allegations as contained in the
petition personally and take necessary steps in accordance with law if
the situation so warrants.
This order shall not be construed to be conferring the
legitimacy or authenticity to the factum of marriage having been
performed as well as the age, as the Court is clearly deprived of any
means to determine the aforesaid facts.

adjudicationQueue.textTail:
ubiya, District Etawah.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the admittedly the victim
is living at her parents' house. He further submits that the allegation
levelled against the petitioners is absolutely false, frivolous and baseless.
From a perusal of the FIR, no offence is made out out against the
petitioners, hence, the same be quashed.
Learned AGA opposed the prayer for quashing of the FIR and submitted
that there is allegation against the petitioners for enticing away the victim
who is a minor girl.
The Full Bench of this Court in Ajit Singh @ Muraha v. State of U.P.
(2006 (56) ACC 433) reiterated the view taken by the earlier Full Bench in
Satya Pal v. State of U.P. (2000 Cr.L.J. 569) after considering the various
decisions including State of Haryana v. Bhajan Lal (AIR 1992 SC 604)
that there can be no interference with the investigation or order staying
arrest unless cognizable offence is not ex-facie discernible from the
allegations contained in the F.I.R. or there is any statutory restriction
operating on the power of the Police to investigate a case.

cognizable offence is made out. Hence no ground exists for quashing of

This writ petition is for issuance of the direction upon
the opposite parties to appoint the petitioner on
compassionate ground under the provision of the
Rehabilitation Assistance Rules, 1990.
The case of the petitioner is that her father, while
working as peon in Panchalingeswar High School, in the
district of Balasore died in harness on 31.07.2016 and as
such, he has made an application for getting appointment
on compassionate ground, but the same has not been
extended in his favour.

petitioner’s case is squarely covered by the judgment
rendered by this Court in the case of Ritanjali
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
M.E. Deptt.) & others,

petitioner is not ventilated by the authorities. Hence, the
instant writ petition has been filed.

and after going through the order passed by this Court in
the case of Ritanjali giri @ Paul (supra) as also the order
dated 21.6.2017 passed by this Court in W.P.(C) No.10073
of 2017, the case of the petitioner required to be considered
by the authorities in the light of the said judgment.

liberty to the petitioner to file a representation before the

the judgments referred in this regard by this Court within

THE HON'BLE SRI JUSTICE K.C. BHANU
CIVIL REVISION PETITION NO. 4214 OF 2009
ORDER:
This Civil Revision Petition under Article 227 of the Constitution
of India, is directed against the order, dated 05.06.2009, in O.S.No.549
of 2007 on the file of Principal Senior Civil Judge, Tirupati,
whereunder and whereby, the Court below returned the document
dated 27.04.2007, for want of Stamp duty and Penalty.
2. Heard
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
uthenticated by any such person or by any public officer, unless such
instrument is duly stamped. This provision categorically provided that
an instrument shall not be admitted for any purpose whatsoever.
6. No doubt, when the document is compulsorily registerble under
Section 17 of the Registration Act, the same is not registered it can be
used for collateral purpose in view of proviso to Section 49 of the
Indian Registration Act. When the stamp duty and penalty has not
been paid, the question of receipt of document cannot be entertained.
Therefore, the trial Court rightly stated that the document is not
admissible in evidence and it requires stamp duty and penalty. To
some extent, the trial Court is correct in saying that the document
requires stamp duty and penalty. For want of registration, the receipt of
document need not be rejected. Therefore, the trial Court ought to
considered the document for collateral purpose in view of proviso to
Section 49 of the Indian Registration Act.
7. Accordingly, the Civil Revision Petition is allowed remanding
the matter to the trial Court directing the petitioner to pay the stamp
duty and penalty as required under Section 35 of the Act. Thereafter,
the said document can be received as evidence in terms of proviso to
Section 49 of the Registration Act. There shall be no order as to costs.

entire proceeding of Sessions Trial
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
nces are made out against
the applicant or not.
4. The Hon'ble Supreme Court in C.B.I. v. Aryan Singh, 2023
SCC Online SC 379 has held that while exercising the powers
under Section 482 Cr.P.C., the Court is not required to conduct
a mini trial. It does not require the prosecution/investigating
agency to prove the allegations. While exercising the powers
under Section 482 of the CrPC the Court has very limited
jurisdiction and is required to consider "whether any sufficient
material available to proceed further against the accused for
which the accused is required to be tried or not".
5. Confronted with the aforesaid objection, the learned counsel
for the applicant submits that he does not want to press this
application on merit and he confines his prayer only to the
extent that applicant may be permitted to surrender and move
an application, before the court concerned seeking bail and
suitable directions may be issued that same may be heard and
decided expeditiously, in accordance to law.
6. Accordingly, the instant application is disposed of by
observing that in case the applicant appears and file an
application for his release on bail, the same shall be considered
and decided expeditiously in accordance with law, including the
law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Satender

encashed.
In such circumstances, the petitioner is bound by the
principle of estoppel and now cannot turn around that he is entitled for
consideration of extension of one year service on account of the
second application having encashed the retiral dues.
Resultantly, there is no merit in the writ petition and the
same stands dismissed.

This writ petition has been filed by the petitioner
challenging the order of cancellation of Fair Price

Muzaffar Nagar.
It is the case of the petitioner that the SDM,
Jansath, District Muzaffar Nagar, who had also
been arrayed as opposite party no. 3 in this writ
petition in his personal capacity, is unduly
influenced and under pressure of respondent nos.
4 to 6, the priv
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
of his rights in a suit or proceeding. If the
Court was of opinion that there' was no other convenient or adequate
remedy open to the petitioners, it might have proceeded to investigate the
case on its merits and come to a decision as to whether the petitioners
succeeded in establishing that there was an infringement of any of their
legal rights which entitled them to a writ of mandamus or any other
directions of a like nature; and pending such determination it might have
made a suitable interim order for maintaining the status quo ante. But
when the Court declined to decide on the rights of the parties and
expressly held that they should be investigated more properly in a civil
suit, it could not, for the purpose of facilitating the institution of such suit,
issue directions in the nature of temporary injunctions, under Article 226
of the Constitution. In our opinion, the language of Article 226 does not
permit such an action. On that short ground the judgment of the Orissa
High Court under appeal cannot be upheld."
In view of the law settled by the Hon'ble Supreme
Court in the case of Madan Gopal Rungta
(supra), if this Court is dismissing the writ petition
as not maintainable in view of the statutory
remedy being available, this Court cannot pass
any interim order in favour of the petitioner.
The writ petition is dismissed. No order as to costs.

adjudicationQueue.textTail:
he time of this recovery, the accused
was hang up and it cannot therefore be said to be a
voluntary recovery as contemplated by section 27.
6. If this recovery is excluded, the circumstances proved are grossly
inadequate to come to the conclusion that the death of the victim was
caused by the accused only.
7. It is an accepted position of law that to sustain a conviction, on
the basis of circumstantial evidence, the prosecution must prove the
(5)
complete chain of circumstances, leading to death. We have already
observed what has been proved by the prosecution. Even the
recovery is held proved. There is nothing to connect the accused
with the crime as the prosecution has not proved the circumstances of
the accused handling the axe in any manner. In the absence of any
ocular testimony that the killing was done by that axe and by the
accused, merely because the axe is recovered at the instance of the
accused, it would be unsafe to sustain the conviction as contended by
the prosecution. In our opinion, the learned Judge has rightly
appreciated the evidence on record and was legally justified in
acquitting the accused. In any event, in our opinion, this is not a case
where this court in its appellate jurisdiction should interfere with the
order of acquittal, which is well reasoned, supported by evidence and
law. In the result, therefore, the appeal fails and it is dismissed,.

the issuance of reopening notice alleging change of opinion on

before this Court. Further, mere pendency of a issue before this

adjudicationQueue.textTail:
returned from the fields upon the message relayed.
Right from beginning, in the bed-head ticket (Exhibit-D/1-D/3)
the case of Prabhu Lal (P.W.1) is that Celphos has been
administered and child was vomiting. The vomit had given
pungent smell. The child had also vomited part of some tablets.
Neither tablet was retained, nor the vomit was saved for the
purpose of test. Immediately, when the child reached at the
hospital, he was given stomach wash and even gastric lavage
fluids were not retained. To us, it is not safe to rely upon the
oral dying declaration made by the deceased Sonu, aged three
years before the parents to convict the appellant, Bhanwari Bai
and since Priya has not stepped into witness box, what is told by
her to the parents, being hearsay, cannot be relied.
43. Be that as it may, since we are of the view that it is
not safe to rely upon the oral dying declaration, we cannot say
with certainty that appellant had administered some substance
to the child, as a matter of abundant caution, we shall extend
the benefit of doubt to the appellant, Bhanwari Bai.
44. Consequently, the appeal is accepted and set aside
the conviction and sentence qua the appellant and she is
acquitted of all the charges.

The petitioner is engaged in the post of ‘Gram

under Tufangunj-I Development Block and has been
working in such post from 16th March, 2015.
Learned Counsel for the petitioner places the
engagement letter dated 29th August, 2011 from the
Pradhan of Nakkatigachh Gram Panchayat, by which
the petitioner was appointed to such post. Counsel
submits that the petitioner made several
re
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
everal

been considered by the authorities. Counsel also
refers to a letter from the office of the Executive
Assistant of Nakkatigachh Gram Panchayat,
enclosing documents of casual workers of Tufangunj-I
Panchayat Samity to the Block Development Officer
Tufangunj-I, Development Block Cooch Behar and the
2
District Panchayat and Rural Development Officer,
which shows that the petitioner’s prayer for being

although there is no difficulty in considering the
representations of the petitioner but there are certain

Hon'ble Saral Srivastava,J.
Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned and Sri
Ashok Kumar Lal, learned counsel for the respondents.
Petitioner by means of present writ petition has prayed for
following reliefs:
"(A) a writ, order or direction in the nature of certiorari quashing the
impugned orders dated 21.03.2020 (Annexure No.1) so far it relates to
awarding of punishment to the petitioner and order dated 05.05.2021
(Annexure No.2) passed by respon
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
l of the petitioner.
Learned Standing Counsel contended that the order impugned is
not a final order rather a provisional order, therefore, appellate
authority has not committed any error in rejecting the appeal of
the petitioner.
Be that as it may, it would be appropriate to reproduce
Regulation No. 86 of Regulations, 1975 to appreciate the
controversy:
"Appeal- Orders imposing penalty under sub-clauses (a) to (d) of clause
(1) of Regulation NO. 84 shall be appealalble to the authorities as
mentioned in Appendix 'D'."
Bare reading of the Regulation 86 discloses that orders
imposing penalty under sub-clauses (a) to (d) of clause 1 of
Regulation No. 84 shall be appealable to the authorities
mentioned in Appendix 'D". Order of withholding of increment
is one of the punishment which can be awarded under
Regulation 84 (iv) of Regulations, 1975. Therefore, the appeal
against the order withholding the increment, is maintainable
and the reason given by the Appellate Authority for dismissing
the appeal on the ground that the order of punishment is not
final in nature, is not sustainable. Therefore, the order of
Appellate Authority dated 18.05.2020 is set aside.
The Appellate Authority is directed to consider the appeal of the
petitioner on merits in accordance with law and decide the same
within one month from the date of production of copy of this
order.
Order Date :- 23.10.2021

Appellant :- Commissioner Of Income Tax (Central)
Respondent :- M/S Rama Educational Society
Counsel for Appellant :- A.N. Mahajan (Sc-It),Dhananjay Awasthi,Gaurav Mahajan,Manish
Goyal,S.S.C. I.T.
Counsel for Respondent :- Ashish Bansal,S.K. Garg
Hon'ble Bharati Sapru,J.
Hon'ble Neeraj Tiwari,J.
Heard Sri Gaurav Mahajan, learned Counsel for the
department and Sri Ashish Bansal, learned Counsel for the
assessee.
This is an appeal filed by the department under Section 260A
of the Income Tax Act, 1961 against an order of the Tribunal
dated 30.12.2009 by which the order passed by the authority
registering the assessee under Section 12A o
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
1.04.2005 on certain grounds that the activities of the
assessee were not being carried on in accordance with the
provisions required to be fulfilled under Section 12A of the
Act.
The Tribunal records a finding that from a perusal of the show
cause notice, which was issued on 29.01.2009 it appears that
the entire proceedings have been initiated on the basis of
doubts. A portion of the show cause notice is quoted
hereunder:-
"A prima-facie case is made out against the Society raising serious doubts
regarding genuineness of the activities of the society. Hence, it is proposed that
the registration granted to the society u/s 12 of the I.T. Act, 1961 be canceled."
The Tribunal, therefore, after examining the matter at length
recorded a finding of fact that since there was no cogent
maltrial or evidence to establish any violation of the
provisions of Section 12AA(3) of the Act the cancellation of
the registration retrospectively was illegal, bad in law and not
justified and, therefore, the Tribunal has set it aside.
In view of the facts and circumstances as discussed by the
Tribunal we are of the opinion that there is no error in the
conclusion reached by the Tribunal. Hence, the order of the
Tribunal is upheld by this Court. The questions of law are
answered in favour of the assessee and against the department.
The appeal is dismissed as above. No costs.
Order Date :- 5.3.2018
S.P.

BEFORE
HON’BLE MR. JUSTICE UJJAL BHUYAN
Heard Mr. DP Chaliha, learned senior counsel for the petitioner and Mr. NJ Khata
niar, learned Standing counsel, Education (Elementary) Department.
By way of this petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, petition
er seeks a direction to the respondents to regularize her service as Assistant T
eacher of No.2104 Jal Bharat Hindi Vidyalaya, Bilasipara in the district of Dhub
ri.
Case of the petitioner is that she was appointed by the Managing Committee of th
e said School as Assistant Teacher with effect from 06-02-1985 and has been disc
harging her duties since then. At the relevant point of time, the School was at
venture
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
e than 10 years of service on honorary basis, her service should
be regularized. In fact the petitioner had approached this Court earlier by fi
ling Civil Rule No.2480/1995 which was disposed of by this Court vide order date
d 21st June, 1995 by directing the Director of Elementary Department, Assam to e
nquire into the claim of the petitioner and thereafter to pass appropriate order
(s). Since no decision has been taken, petitioner has filed the present writ pe
tition.
An affidavit has been filed on behalf of the Director of Elementary Education, A
ssam. In the affidavit it is stated that petitioner was appointed as honorary t
eacher in the School by the School Managing Committee on 04-02-1988 but was give
n effect from 06-02-1985. Petitioner’s appointment was after provincialisation
of the School. The School was provincialised on 01-06-1977. After provincialis
ation, the selection and appointment of teachers would be governed by the provis
ions of Assam Elementary Education (Provincialisation) Rules, 1977. The School
Managing Committee could not have made appointment of the petitioner which is il
legal.
The stand taken by the Director has been upheld by this Court in the case of Jah
angir Alam & Ors. Vs. State of Assam & Ors. reported in 2003 (3) GLT 544.
That being the position, claim of the petitioner lacks substance and is accordin
gly rejected.
Writ petition is dismissed.

* * *
HON’BLE SRI JUSTICE N.R.L. NAGESWARA RAO
CRIMINAL APPEAL No.1265 of 2004
JUDGMENT:
This appeal is filed against discharge of the
accused in C.C. No.116 of 1999 on the file of XI
Metropolitan Magistrate, Secunderabad.
2. A private complaint for the offences under Sections
406 and 420 IPC was filed against seven (7) accused
persons and some of the accused persons appeared and
some accused did not appear. After taking the case on
file, for several
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
ssary and
consequently the discharge recorded by the court below
is not proper.
5. As can be seen from the record, the case was taken
on file in the year 1999 and the complainant and the
accused were attending the court and at no point of time
during the year 2001 the complainant has gone into the
box to give evidence though accused were present.
Subsequently, the complainant was also not present
before the court on 10.3.2001. On 08.6.2001 both parties
were present and on 29.6.2001 both parties were absent
and there was no representation for the complainant. On
20.7.2001, 31.5.2002, 16.8.2002, 05.12.2002, 07.12.2002
and 24.01.2003 the complainant was absent and
ultimately on 26.9.2003 and subsequently also the
complainant was absent.
6. From the above material it is quite clear that the
complainant was not present continuously and it is the
duty of the complainant to see that steps are properly
taken for apprehension of the accused and when the
complainant himself fails to appear properly, it is not the
duty of the court to show more indulgence than what has
been shown by the court below. I do not find any reason
to interfere with the order of discharge.
7. The criminal appeal is accordingly dismissed.
_____________________________

The instant review application has been filed praying for review

petitions leading petition being Writ Petition No. 5221 (SS) of
2013 in re: Siddharth Narain Dixit vs State of U.P. and
others in which the writ petition filed by the petitioners namely
Writ Petition No. 6989 (SS) of 2014 in re: Mahraj Deen

adjudicationQueue.textTail:
andamus and the respondents were to approach the
authorities for redressal of the their grievance, disposed of the
petitions leaving it open to the petitioners to approach the
respondents for redressal of grievances regarding payment of
pay scale as have been paid to their counterparts.
The instant review petition has been filed contending that in
other matters the view of the State Government is already
known by which the claim of the petitioners similarly
circumstanced had been rejected as such once the view of the
government is known consequently the petitioners are not
willing to go before the government for redressal of their
grievances and are now before this Court praying to entertain
the review petition.
The Court is of the view that once the petitioners have
admittedly never approached the State Government for
redressal of their grievances and in certain other cases the claim
of those persons has been rejected, as such the rejection of the
claim in other cases cannot be said to be an error apparent on
the face of record. of the judgement passed by this Court in the
case of Siddharth Narain Dixit (supra) and in the case of the
petitioners also so as to entertain the review petition.
Considering the aforesaid, the review petition is dismissed.

8.1.2007
HON'BLE MR. JUSTICE MOHAMMAD RAFIQ
Shri M.C. Gupta on behalf of Shri P.L.
Agarwal for the petitioner.
Shri V.K. Mathur for respondent No.2.
Shri B.S. Chhaba, Dy. G.A.
Petitioner in this writ petition, has
challenged the order passed by the
Rajasthan Non-Government Educational
Institutions, Tribunal, Jaipur dated
20.5.2002, whereby the Tribunal had directed
the petitioner Institution to make payment
of gratuity together with interest @ 9%
p.a. to the respondent No.2.
Learned counsel for the respondents has
cited judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court
in
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
s has
cited judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court
in Rajasthan Welfare Society v/s State of
Rajasthan (2005 CDR 446 (SC) in which the
Hon'ble Supreme Court has held that the
gratuity within the meaning of the
Rajasthan Non-Government Educational
Institutions Act, 1989 and the Rajasthan
Non-Government Educational Institutions
(Recognition, Grant-in-aid and Service
Conditions etc.) Rules, 1993, cannot form
part of recurring grant. It is not
includable as part of approved expenditure
for the purposes of computing the amount of
grant payable to the appellant. It was
however held that teachers of Non-Government
education Institution are entitled to
payment of gratuity. The Hon'ble Supreme
Court in para 17 of the judgment has
granted the liberty to the concerned
educational institution that if the
representations are made by added Non-
Government Educational Institutions, the
State Government would consider
sympathetically the question of the gratuity
amount payable to the employees being taken
into consideration for the purpose of
computing the amount of grant-in-aid.
In view of the aforesaid judgment, I do
not find any good reason to interfere with
the order passed by the Tribunal. The writ
petition is dismissed. The petitioner may
if it so desire, make a representation to
the Government in terms of the observations
made in para 17 of the judgment supra

By this common order the aforementioned two Letters Patent
Appeals i.e. LPA-1968-2025 and LPA-1969-2025 are being decided. For the
sake of convenience, the facts have been taken from LPA
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
)(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act.
The Labour Court ought to have relegated respondent No.2 to initiate
appropriate proceedings by way of reference and get his right
crystalized and/or adjudicate upon. Therefore, the order passed by the
Labour Court was beyond the jurisdiction conferred under Section
33(C)(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act. The High Court has not
appreciated the aforesaid facts and has confirmed the same without
adverting to the scope and ambit of the jurisdiction of the Labour
Court under Section 33(C)(2) of the Industrial Disputes Act.”
6. The judgments relied upon by the learned counsel for the appellant
are distinguishable on facts and do not help the case of the appellant in any
manner whatsoever. In those cases, it was held that if the workmen therein had
completed 240 days of service, they would be entitled to regularization and
they do not pertain adjudication under Section 33 (C) (2) of the Industrial
Disputes Act, 1947.
7. Consequently, we are of the considered view that there is no
illegality in the judgment of the Single Bench warranting interference in letters
patent appeal.
8. Both the above-mentioned Letters Patent Appeals stand dismissed.

JUDGMENT:
This appeal is filed questioning the order dated 30.05.2016 in
I.A.No.170 of 2016 in O.S.No.80 of 2016 on the file of Vacation Civil
Judge, City Civil Court, Hyderabad.
2. The appellants herein are plaintiffs, who filed the above
referred suit for the relief of permanent injunction, and they filed
I.A.No.170 of 2016 seeking temporary injunction and Vacation Civil
Court by impugned order dated 30.05.2016 dismissed the application.
3. Heard advocate for appellants, party-in-
person/respondent No.2 and advocate for respondent No.1.
4. Advocate for appellants mainly contended that Vacation
Civil Court, w
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
ondent No.1 submitted that sufficient
opportunity was given to appellants and as the Vacation was coming
to an end Court decided the matter on merits and that there is nothing
wrong in the procedure adopted by Court below.
7. Considering the submissions of both sides, without going
into any of the points raised by both sides, since on a bare looking at
the order of the Court below, I am of the view that it cannot be treated
as an order on merits and Court below only decided the matter by
looking into the documents and contentions of one party. Therefore, I
feel that it is a fit case where the impugned order has to be set aside
and the matter has to be sent back to the Court below for fresh
consideration by fixing some time schedule.
8. For these reasons, the impugned order dated 30.05.2016
is set aside and the matter is remitted back to Court below directing it
to dispose of the same within four weeks from the date of receipt of a
copy of this order, taking into consideration the documents of both
parties and without being prejudiced by any of the observations made
in its earlier order.

adjudicationQueue.textTail:

person accused of an offence punishable under Section 379 IPC is
convicted, the vehicle is not liable for confiscation. However, since the
vehicle is the subject matter of the criminal case, it has to be preserved

By means of this writ petition under Article 226 of the Constitution of India, the
petitioners are seeking relief in the nature of mandamus commanding the
respondents to regularize the petitioner on Group 'D' posts as they are working
since 1990.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has placed reliance upon the Government
Order dated 29.02.2008 according to which the employees working on daily
wage basis in the local bodies and whose appointments hav
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
06.1991 and have been working on 21.12.2001, shall be absorbed on a
permanent post or temporary vacancy that may exist in the local bodies.
Sri Sant Ram Sharma appearing for respondent nos. 3 and 4 admits that the
petitioners have been working with the Nagar Palika Parishad, Banda since prior
to 29.06.1991 and are still working and are being paid salary of the minimum
pay scale admissible to Group 'D' positions.
Since the Government Order dated 29.02.2008 creates obligation upon local
bodies to absorb the daily wage employees working in local bodies against
existing, permanent or temporary positions in the local bodies, I therefore, direct
the 3rd and 4th respondents to consider the claim of the petitioners for
regularization/ absorption against the vacancies permanent or temporary existing
in the Nagar Palika Parishad in the light of Government Order dated 29.02.2008.
The necessary exercise shall be done within a period of three months from the
date of production of certified copy of this order. It is further made clear that in
the event if no such vacancy exists with Nagar Palika Parishad, Banda, the
petitioners shall be absorbed as and when such vacancies are created by virtue of
retirement or sanction by the Government in the light of Government Order
(supra).
The writ petition is disposed of with the aforesaid observations and directions.

* * *
Present: Mr. B.D. Sharma, Advocate for the petitioners.
* * *
Rakesh Kumar Garg, J.(Oral)
This is defendants' revision petition challenging the orders
dated 20.10.2008 and 25.2.2009 passed by the Civil Judge (Jr. Division),
Amritsar and the Additional District Judge, Amritsar respectively vide
which application of the petitioners filed under Order 39 Rules 1 and 2 CPC
restraining the respondents from alienating the property in dispute during
adjudicationQueue.textTail:
operty in dispute during the pendency of the suit was also
filed which has been dismissed by the Courts below vide impugned
orders.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has vehemently argued
that admittedly, the property in dispute is joint and therefore, the petitioners
CR No.3083 of 2009(O&M) -2-
shall suffer irreparable loss and injury in case the respondents are not
restrained from alienating the property in dispute during the pendency of
the suit.
I have heard learned counsel for the petitioners.
A perusal of the impugned orders would show that the plaintiff-
petitioners while filing this suit and the application for ad interim injunction
have not disclosed that a loan was availed of from Canara Bank and the
aforesaid Bank has already taken possession of the property and has put
the same to sale for the recovery of an amount of Rs.60,59,467/-. Thus,
finding the petitioners guilty of concealment of material facts, the Courts
below held that the petitioners were not entitled to discretionary relief of an
injunction.
Moreover, I find from the perusal of the record of the revision
petition that there is even no averment made by the petitioners that the
respondents are alienating the suit property. Even otherwise also doctrine
of lis pendens will apply to the alienation, if any.
Thus, I find no merit in this revision petition.
Dismissed.
May 27, 2009 (RAKESH KUMAR GARG)
ps JUDGE

caveats: Draws are uniform over judgments.id, which is uuid v4. If ids ever stop being uniformly distributed — a sequential or time-ordered id scheme, a bulk load with a fixed prefix — this sampler silently stops being uniform and nothing here would notice.

The eligibility predicate is transcribed into JavaScript so that admission can be attributed to a single conjunct, which SQL cannot report. The deployed view hash is recorded above; if it differs from the hash in the report that quoted this run, the transcription must be re-read before any number here is trusted. It has already drifted once: migration 0066 made bail orders reachable and added semantic_tier, and this file was updated to follow rather than the other way round.

admitted now means "the view gives this row a tier other than NOT_ELIGIBLE". Before migration 0066 it meant that AND not a bail order, so an admitted count from this tool taken before 21 Aug 2026 is over a smaller population by roughly the bail share.
text_len saturates at 200,000 characters. Every band boundary the predicate uses is far below that, so bands are exact; a mean length computed from this field is not.

The marker screen fires on the head and tail only, not on the whole document. Its recall on a truncated probe is lower than the 76.2% measured on full text, so the legacy-font rate reported here is a FLOOR.

HIGH-CONFIDENCE SUBSTANTIVE, NON-SUBSTANTIVE and UNCERTAIN are deliberately NOT assigned mechanically. A row reading PENDING_ADJUDICATION has not been judged, and counting those as substantive would restate the selector as its own audit.
